content.narration: The morning air is crisp. By the fire, Aitor inspects the tip of his spear while Bor sharpens a large flint knife. Unai approaches them, holding several newly-knapped spear points.

dialogue.line: These are ready. The flint from the upper quarry is good.
They are well-made, Unai. Sharp and balanced. They will fly true.
Hah! Give me the biggest one. If we find bison today, I want to make sure it feels it!
Patience, Bor. We follow the tracks, not our own noise. We leave when the sun is higher.

schedule.content: A group of women, including Lurra, Amaia, and Nerea, sit together in the sunlit area of the cave mouth. The rhythmic sound of scraping fills the air as they work on a large deer hide stretched across a frame. Their conversation is a low, steady murmur, punctuated by occasional laughter.

content.narration: As darkness settles, the main fire crackles, casting dancing shadows on the cave walls. Zahar sits on a smooth stone, his old eyes reflecting the flames. The children, Sua, Nahia, and Gorka, gather at his feet.

dialogue.line: Yes! Tell us about the Great Hart with antlers of fire!
Hush now, little ones. Tonight is not a night for fire, but for ice. I will tell you of the time the Great Glacier tried to swallow the sun...
Bigger than mountains, Gorka. Now, listen closely...

schedule.content: A sharp crack echoes from the Flint Quarry. Oihan, trying to impress the older knappers, has struck a large nodule too hard, shattering it uselessly. Unai looks over, shakes his head slowly, and wordlessly hands the boy a smaller, more appropriate stone to practice on.

content.narration: Near the edge of the main living area, away from the central fire, Harkaitz and Ederra are speaking in low, tense tones.

dialogue.line: You were watching her again. At the river.
I watch everyone, Ederra. That is my purpose. To guard.
She is unmarried. She wanders far. She is a risk. I watch the risks. That is all.

schedule.content: In the Berry Thicket, Amaia and Bihotz are gathering the last of the season's fruit. Their baskets are nearly full. Amaia points out a particular plant to the younger woman, explaining which leaves can be crushed to make a poultice for stings.
